ac:rich-text-body.p: Audience: Developers working on Java/Maven applications using this CI/CD pipeline.

Goal: After reading this once, you should know exactly which branch to commit to, what version to expect in your build, what the Jenkins parameters do, and where your artifact will land - without asking anyone.

ul.li: Commit your daily work to master. Every PR merge produces a -SNAPSHOT artifact deployable to Dev / UAT only.
Production releases come from release/X.Y branches, not from master.
A release manager cuts a release/X.Y branch by running the master pipeline manually with PROMOTE_DEV=true.
A release manager produces a production-ready build by running the release-branch pipeline manually with PROMOTE_RELEASE=true.
Snapshots never reach STG/Pre-PRD/PRD-Beta/PRD. Releases never reach Dev/UAT. The two worlds are kept strictly apart by which Artifactory repository the artifact lives in.
If you find a bug in production, branch from release/X.Y (not master), fix, PR back to release/X.Y. The fix gets shipped as the next patch (e.g., 1.1.1 -> 1.1.2).
After a release ships to PRD, cherry-pick the release-branch fixes back into master.

p: That's it. The rest of this document explains the why and the corner cases.

tr.td: Stabilization for one minor release line

p: We follow Semantic Versioning - MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

tr.td: New release line cut from master
Each release shipped from release branch

ul.li: pom.xml version always ends in -SNAPSHOT, e.g., 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT.
The MINOR digit reflects the next release line that will be cut from master, not the previous one.

tr.td: Maven builds the artifact at version 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT
Available for deployment to Dev / UAT

p: Nothing else. No tags, no version bumps, no Git pushes. As a developer this is the only path you'll ever invoke directly.
This is the rare one - it cuts a new release line. After this runs:

ul.li: A new branch release/1.1 exists at remote.
Tag 1.1.0 exists, pointing at the commit where master was.
Artifactory local-release has 1.1.0.
Master is now at 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT and ready to receive new development.
release/1.1 is at 1.1.1-SNAPSHOT and ready for stabilization.

ac:rich-text-body.p: Important: the same commit is the parent of both master's 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT bump and release/1.1's 1.1.1-SNAPSHOT bump. The two histories diverge from there.

p: The release branch pipeline has the exact same shape as the master pipeline (standard build vs. promotion), but the promotion does something different: it produces a release artifact instead of cutting a new branch.

ul.li: pom.xml version is X.Y.Z-SNAPSHOT where Z is the next patch to be released.
The MINOR digit is frozen - it will never change on this branch. Only PATCH moves.

h3: 7.2 Bug Found in PRD (after release shipped)
p: Same procedure as above. The only difference is that production is running the broken version, so urgency is higher. The branch, fix, PR, promote, deploy sequence is identical - what would have been 1.1.2 for a regression becomes 1.1.3 because some other patch already shipped between releases.

tr.td: Branch from master to fix a release bug
Master may have new features that aren't in production yet - they'd ship along with your fix.
Open a PR from feature/* -> release/X.Y
PR review and CI gates apply to release-line code too.
Otherwise the next minor release will reintroduce the bug.
Bump the version yourself in a fix PR
Manual version bumps cause merge conflicts and break the pipeline's atomic version-bump step.

tr.td: Dev opens PR with feature A, merged
Dev opens PR with feature B, merged
QA tests 1.1.0-SNAPSHOT on UAT, signs off
Release manager runs master pipeline manually with PROMOTE_DEV=true
Pipeline switches back to master, bumps

p: While 1.1.0 is in STG, QA finds a regression. We need to ship a fix.

tr.td: Dev implements fix, opens PR -> release/1.1, merges
Release manager runs release pipeline with PROMOTE_RELEASE=true
Pipeline tags Git as 1.1.1, bumps to next snapshot
Deploy 1.1.1 through STG -> PRD-Beta -> Pre-PRD -> PRD
Cherry-pick the regression fix from release/1.1 to master

h3: Phase 5 - Bug Found in PRD After 1.1.1 Ships
p: Identical procedure. The next promotion produces 1.1.2. The release branch ends at 1.1.3-SNAPSHOT afterward.
release/1.1 is deleted. Tags 1.1.0, 1.1.1, 1.1.2 remain in Git forever. Master has long since moved on to 1.3.0-SNAPSHOT or beyond.
h3: "I want to add a new feature."
p: Open a PR against master. After merge you'll get a 1.x.0-SNAPSHOT artifact in local-dev. Done.
h3: "I want my feature in the next production release."
p: Get it merged to master before a release manager runs PROMOTE_DEV. Once the release branch is cut, master moves on to the next minor - your feature won't ship in the just-cut release.
h3: "I found a bug in production. How do I fix it?"
p: Branch feature/fix-xyz from release/X.Y (the active release branch). Fix it. PR back to release/X.Y. The release manager will promote when ready.
h3: "I found a bug in production but the release branch was already deleted."
p: That means it's been more than two months since the release shipped, and a newer release line has likely superseded it. The fix path is now: branch from the current release/X.Y, fix, ship. If the bug is in production but the fix is on master only, escalate - we may need to cut a new release line off the affected tag.
No. All code reaches master via PR. The pipeline will build whatever lands there, but the team policy requires PR review.
h3: "Can I commit directly to a release branch?"
p: Same answer - PR only.
h3: "I just merged a fix to release/1.1. Where's the 1.1.2 release?"
p: 1.1.2 doesn't exist yet. Standard PR-merge builds produce snapshots. Here's what's actually happening:

ul.li: Right after 1.1.1 was promoted, the release branch was bumped to 1.1.2-SNAPSHOT.
Your PR-merge builds publish 1.1.2-SNAPSHOT artifacts to local-dev.
When the release manager runs PROMOTE_RELEASE, that snapshot becomes 1.1.2 in local-release.

p: So the snapshot version on the release branch always tells you the next patch number - not the previous one.
h3: "What if my PR to release/1.1 conflicts with something that's already on master?"
p: That's expected - release branch and master have diverged. Resolve the conflict in your fix branch. Don't merge master into release/1.1.
h3: "How do I deploy my SNAPSHOT to STG to test it?"
p: You can't. SNAPSHOTs are blocked from STG by design. Test on Dev/UAT instead. If you genuinely need a STG-quality build, you need a release artifact, which means asking the release manager to promote.
h3: "I see two pom.xml versions in my git log around a release. What happened?"
p: PROMOTE_* does two version commits in one pipeline run:

ol.li: Strip -SNAPSHOT (e.g., 1.1.1-SNAPSHOT -> 1.1.1) - the commit that gets tagged.
Bump to next snapshot (e.g., 1.1.1 -> 1.1.2-SNAPSHOT) - the commit you'll see at HEAD afterward.

p: This is normal. Don't try to undo the second one.
h3: "Can a snapshot ever go to PRD?"
p: No. The pipeline rejects it. The deploy jobs reject it. There is no override.
h3: "Can a release artifact ever go to Dev/UAT?"
p: Also no. Dev/UAT pull from local-dev, which only contains snapshots.
h3: "I see 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT on master but the latest production is 1.1.1. Is master ahead?"
p: Yes - by design. Once release/1.1 is cut, master immediately bumps to the next minor (1.2.0-SNAPSHOT) so any new development going to master is clearly destined for the future 1.2.0 release line. The currently-shipping production version (1.1.x) lives on release/1.1.
